title: Soft-Body Fashion Studio: Dress the Fox & Statue
description: A soft-body physics playground where a Fox and the Nemetona statue stand on pedestals. The user must drag oversized jelly-like sunglasses onto each character, deform them to fit using soft-body spring controls, adjust elasticity and damping per object, and use undo/redo to perfect the look. Energy conservation is tracked as soft-body potential energy must stay within budget.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a soft-body fashion studio. Load Fox.glb on the left pedestal and nemetona.glb on the right pedestal using GLTFLoader. Load SunglassesKhronos.glb twice as two independent soft-body instances, each represented by a mass-spring mesh: duplicate each vertex as a point mass connected by spring constraints to neighbors. Place both sunglasses copies floating above the scene. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,2,5) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Lighting: one DirectionalLight, one AmbientLight, and a soft SpotLight on each pedestal. Interaction steps (10-14 total): (1) Click a sunglasses copy to select it (outline highlight). (2) Drag it toward the Fox or statue using raycaster drag. (3) On drop near a character's head, snap-attach with spring anchors. (4) Use a slider panel to adjust spring stiffness (0.1-2.0) causing the soft-body sunglasses to deform and conform to the head shape. (5) Adjust damping slider (0.01-0.5) controlling oscillation settling. (6) Repeat steps 1-5 for the second sunglasses on the other character. (7) A real-time energy bar displays total elastic potential energy across all springs; it must stay below a threshold (conservation law). If exceeded, sunglasses flash red and user must reduce stiffness. (8) Ctrl+Z triggers undo (reverts last parameter change or placement), Ctrl+Shift+Z triggers redo, maintaining a history stack of at least 10 states. (9) A 'Jiggle' button applies a random impulse to all point masses to test stability. (10) A 'Snapshot' button freezes the simulation and displays a score based on how well sunglasses conform (overlap distance) and energy budget remaining. Implement the mass-spring soft-body simulation in a requestAnimationFrame loop using Verlet integration. Each spring applies Hooke's law force. Store positions in Float32Array and update BufferGeometry each frame. The UI panel should use HTML/CSS overlays with sliders, undo/redo buttons, jiggle button, snapshot button, and the energy bar. Ground plane with shadow-receiving material. All interactions must use raycasting for selection and drag.
